prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
The drawer at the bottom of many refrigerators has a job that is easy to miss.

It may have two settings: low humidity and high humidity. Some models use a slider to change the setting.

These settings control how much air moves through the drawer. The low-humidity side lets more air move. The high-humidity side keeps more moisture inside.

That difference matters because fresh food can lose quality in two ways.

Some foods release a natural gas called ethylene. If other produce stays around this gas too long, it may become overripe and spoil sooner. Other foods lose water quickly. Then they become soft, dry, or wilted.

So the real question is not simply, “Is this a fruit or a vegetable?”

The better question is: “What is the bigger risk for this food?”

【Point One】
For foods that release a lot of ethylene, the low-humidity side can help the gas move away. Apples and pears are examples.

For foods that lose water quickly, the high-humidity side helps keep moisture inside. Leafy greens, such as kale, and broccoli fit this group.

This gives us a simple way to think about unfamiliar produce. Do not put every fruit in one group and every vegetable in another. Think about what will damage that food first: too much ethylene nearby or too much water loss.

【Point Two】
Before choosing a drawer, decide whether the food should go in the refrigerator at all.

Tomatoes and bananas are recommended for room-temperature storage, not refrigerator storage. Potatoes, sweet potatoes, onions, and garlic do not need refrigeration; they are best kept in a cool, dry place.

Also, there is no single household rule for every food. Official and appliance guides do not agree about the best crisper setting for strawberries and oranges. So a humidity slider cannot solve every storage question.
